parts.text:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: In the univariate analysis, vitamin D levels showed no significant association with depression or other geriatric assessment variables, apart from hypertension.
Sentence: "In univariate analysis, no significant associations were found between vitamin D and other variables, except for hypertension (p = 0.049)."
Measured as: depression (geriatric assessment)
Population: Elderly individuals aged 65-100 years receiving home healthcare services
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Vitamin D categories (severe deficiency, deficiency, other groups)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 439
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher vitamin D levels at 12-20 weeks were associated with lower BDI depressive symptom scores at 12-20 weeks' gestation.
Sentence: "We found that vitamin D levels at 12-20 weeks were inversely associated with BDI scores both at 12-20 and at 34-36 weeks' gestation (P < 0.05, both)."
Measured as: BDI scores at 12-20 weeks
Population: Pregnant women from Michigan at risk for depression (by EPDS score or history of depression)
Intervention: Maternal serum vitamin D level measured at 12-20 weeks (observational, not assigned)
Comparator: Lower vs higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 117
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
